detail.abstract: We investigate the trade-off policymakers face between raising tax revenues for public good provision and mitigating the distortionary effects of taxation when individuals can evade taxes and allocate work hours between legal and clandestine (illicit) activities. These distortions lower the constrained optimal tax rate and result in the under-provision of the public good. This under-provision problem is mitigated when surplus from the audit agency is seamlessly transferred to the taxing authorities. Extensions of the basic model incorporate agent heterogeneity and a more general specification of the concealment cost function for infringements.

title: From Neighbors to Components: The Equivalence of Fairness for Neighbors and Gap Preservation
affiliations: Kyushu University

detail.title: From Neighbors to Components: The Equivalence of Fairness for Neighbors and Gap Preservation
detail.abstract: This paper investigates fairness principles in cooperative games with communication graphs. We show that several axioms-fairness for neighbors (Béal et al., 2012), splitting (Casajus, 2009), and a new axiom called gap preservation-are equivalent. Moreover, we show that fairness for neighbors, combined with either component efficiency or a weaker locality condition, guarantees the existence of a pairwise stable communication graph.

title: The Information Content of The Implied Volatility Surface: How to More Efficiently Use Option Information to Predict Stock Returns?
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Charlotte - Finance, Cornerstone Research and University of Texas at Dallas

detail.title: The Information Content of The Implied Volatility Surface: How to More Efficiently Use Option Information to Predict Stock Returns?
detail.abstract: Applying the partial least squares (PLS) approach to the entire implied volatility(IV) surface, we show that option prices contain valuable information about futuredownward jumps in the underlying stock prices, resulting in strong return predictabil-ity. A long-short portfolio based on the extracted downward jump signal yields anannual return of 18.36% with a Sharpe ratio of 1.29. The predictive power of this sig-nal is highly robust and fully subsumes that of other IV-related predictors, highlightingthe significant efficiency gains from exploiting the entire IV surface. Finally, we showthat the predictability aligns with the notion that informed investors trade options toprofit from large negative price movements, circumventing the short-sale constraint inthe equity market.

title: Cyclicality in the Prices of Risk What More Can We Learn from Explainable AI?1
affiliations: McMaster University - Michael G. DeGroote School of Business and McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management

detail.title: Cyclicality in the Prices of Risk What More Can We Learn from Explainable AI?1
detail.abstract: We uncover the temporal patterns of risk premia through portfolios with varying sensitivities to the economic and financial cycles. The highs and lows of the cycle contribute to the statistical significance of intertemporal risk. Its price decreases during an economic downturn, unlike market risk, but increases under tight funding conditions. Predictive machine learning models and their SHAP values suggest that a limited number of firm characteristics convey the most informative signals about these prices of risk and their effect on asset risk premia. In the time series, return characteristics become crucial during recessions periods. In the cross-section, Valuation ratios are more important determinants for Cyclical relative to Defensive industries.

title: Monetary Policy Announcements with Resolution
affiliations: Capital University of Economics and Business, ISEM and Capital University of Economics and Business, ISEM

detail.title: Monetary Policy Announcements with Resolution
detail.abstract: When the FOMC announces its policy decisions with a clear objective and a projected rate path, monetary policy uncertainty declines, amplifying financial markets' reactions to policy surprises. In particular, short- and long-term Treasury yields, risk appetite, and private credit spreads respond more strongly to monetary policy surprises with clearly-perceived policy resolution. As a consequence, economic activity is significantly affected through the ``risk-taking'' channel of monetary policy transmission. These findings are obtained from a novel resolution factor extracted from high-frequency asset prices, including the implied volatility of future interest rate, around FOMC announcements.

title: The Cryptocurrency Gender Gap
affiliations: King's Business School, King's College London, ESC Rennes School of Business, University of Reading - ICMA Centre, Henley Business School, Rennes School of Business and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Cryptocurrency Gender Gap
detail.abstract: Our unique survey of over 1,500 online retail investors in Denmark, Finland and Sweden provides empirical evidence for the pronounced gender gap in cryptocurrency participation. Men are 13% points more likely than women to be current participants, and they have higher intentions to buy cryptos in the future. Several factors, including cryptocurrency knowledge and risk appetite, regulatory perceptions, and economic optimism influence these differences. Our results confirm that the pervasive gender differences in stock market participation extend to the more volatile and less regulated cryptocurrency market but that, given the attenuating effects of other factors, gender cannot be considered in isolation. This, in combination with the rapidly evolving fintech space, emphasize the need for regulators and other stakeholders to ensure that all consumers are sufficiently informed to make appropriate investment decisions, especially in these novel assets.

title: The Ministructure of a Financial Asset
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Ministructure of a Financial Asset
detail.abstract:
The gaps that occur between the closing and subsequent reopening of 1-minute candles are a phenomenon studied in financial literature and included within the so-called market microstructure. This literature addresses these types of gaps from different perspectives, ranging from the distinction between a jump and market noise, their causes and characteristics, to their application in the financial market for the detection of informative events and relevant news, risk and volatility modeling, the prediction of immediate price movements, or the detection of executions or cancellations of large market orders.

Based on this, the present study offers a new application that is unprecedented to date and represents a revolution in the conception of these gaps in terms of technical analysis. Given that these gaps are capable of marking short-term highs and lows, both from a price and seasonality perspective, they constitute a new pattern that traders can take advantage of.

title: Risk And Asset Allocation For Pensions

detail.title: Risk And Asset Allocation For Pensions
detail.abstract:
We provide a comprehensive framework for navigating the complex trade-offs in pension liability management. We use long-term cashflow projections that-over the market probability distribution-pay liabilities from assets while maintaining a target allocation to quantify the importance of choices. The asset allocation and the required funding that it entails are the dominant drivers. Contrary to conventional wisdom, low risk over the long-term stems from high-yield assets rather than low-volatility ones. When and how to extract capital not needed to pay liabilities and costs, called surplus, is a key choice.

An optimal allocation holds 55% private equity, 20% other private capital, and 25% low-risk assets like government bonds for liquidity purposes. For a conservative risk appetite such allocation requires funding around 65% of LIAB0 (undiscounted liabilities), compared to 80% for a more traditional allocation (35% bonds, 35% equity and 30% private capital) and 92% for bonds-only. Time-varying allocations are consistently detrimental.

Surplus extraction mechanisms have limited long-term impact. Fees, an unconditional form of extraction, favor the pension company more than the pensioners. Delays increase undiscounted surplus but reduce value on capital invested by the pension company. Extracting all capital above 83% LIAB0 or 135% LIABIFRS  (3.5%discounted) or 110% LIABHGB (1.9%discounted) is viable either without fees and a few years delay or with 0.2% fees and ten years delay. Annual partial extraction raises the effective extraction threshold unnecessary. Smoother extraction mechanisms are less transparent and yield comparable long-term results.

Key liability risks – such as inflation and mortality assumptions - are best addressed by stress tests with alternative liabilities as prescribed by a risk appetite. Costs, of the order of 5% of LIAB0, are also material. Assumptions and model uncertainty is also addressed by stress tests.

A liability transfer at 62%-LIAB0 (currently LIABIFRS) plus a modest 3%-LIAB0 addition by the pension company is a win-win-win proposal for the pensioners, transferring firm and pension company.

This applies to DB-schemes but the principles on risk and allocation apply to DC as well.

title: Is There a Life-Cycle in Dual-Class Valuation? Evidence from Interwar Belgium
affiliations: Ghent University, Monash University and University of Antwerp

detail.title: Is There a Life-Cycle in Dual-Class Valuation? Evidence from Interwar Belgium
detail.abstract: We examine whether there is a life-cycle in dual-class valuation. Using interwar Belgium as a laboratory, we exploit two governance shocks: the Brussels Stock Exchange’s public naming and shaming of dual-class firms in March 1930, and the abolishment of dual-class shares in October 1934. We find that for firms that introduced dual-class equity after incorporation (mostly after their IPO), the naming and shaming negatively affected the stock price, while after the abolishment of dual-class equity the stock price increased significantly. In contrast, shareholders value insider control by founders as the naming and shaming had no impact on the stock price for firms with dual-class equity already at incorporation, while the 1934 Abolishment Act reduced their stock prices. These findings confirm that investors perceived dual-class equity as an expropriation tool for mature firms, but not for younger firms.

title: Bio-Efficacy of Indigenous Weed-Derived Botanical Insecticides Against Fall Armyworm (FAW) Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
affiliations: Cagayan State University, Cagayan State University, Cagayan State University, Cagayan State University, Cagayan State University and Cagayan State University

detail.title: Bio-Efficacy of Indigenous Weed-Derived Botanical Insecticides Against Fall Armyworm (FAW) Spodoptera frugiperda (J.E. Smith) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
detail.abstract: The present study investigates the insecticidal properties and chemical composition of three native Philippine weeds, Lantana camara, Chromolaena odorata, and Hyptis suaveolens against Spodoptera frugiperda, a critical pest in maize cultivation. Through controlled lab bioassays, the effects of botanical extracts on larval mortality, pupation, and adult emergence were assessed. Phytochemical tests confirmed the presence of key bioactive substances, including flavonoids, phenols, tannins, and terpenoids, while saponins were notably absent in H. suaveolens. Using probit analysis, both LC₅₀ and LT₅₀ values were calculated. Among treatments, L. camara exhibited the most potent insecticidal effects, outperforming other botanicals in mortality and developmental disruption metrics. While cypermethrin remained most effective overall, findings suggest L. camara could be a practical, eco-friendly alternative. Further research should explore field applications and advanced formulations for sustainable pest control strategies.

title: Option-Based Portfolio Insurance Over a Rolling Window: Introduction and Derivation by Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: Lombard Odier & Cie

detail.title: Option-Based Portfolio Insurance Over a Rolling Window: Introduction and Derivation by Reinforcement Learning

publicationDetails.detailsText: The Journal of Financial Data Science, volume 6, issue 2, 2024[10.3905/jfds.2024.1.151]

detail.abstract:
Among various portfolio insurance strategies, Option-based portfolio insurance (OBPI) stands out as the unique strategy offering both downside protection and minimum upside participation. Its
implementation, however, is challenging for public funds, whose investors have different entry points and uncertain holding periods. In this paper, we extend OBPI to ensure downside protection over a rolling window. Such an objective reflects the common practice where the performance of funds is regularly monitored over fixed time intervals. We show how to derive the optimal strategy using methods of reinforcement learning, and demonstrate that it provides a more effective portfolio
protection than the existing methods both on simulated and real-life data.

title: Depression and Biological Markers: Evidence from the British Household Panel Survey
affiliations: , University of Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh - School of Social and Political Science

detail.title: Depression and Biological Markers: Evidence from the British Household Panel Survey

declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any funding.

keywords: Biological Confounding JEL Classification Codes: I12

detail.abstract: This investigation examines the fundamental question of whether the well-documented socioeconomic gradient in depression represents genuine social causation or reflects underlying biological confounding mechanisms. Using longitudinal data from the British Household Panel Survey, we implement a multi-stage econometric strategy. First, gender-stratified Ordered Probit models dissect the socioeconomic gradient of depression. Second, we integrate a panel of biological markers to test for associative effects and bio-psychosocial interactions. Finally, an Instrumental Variable (IV) Probit model, which uses exogenous variation in blood sample processing delay as an instrument, aims to improve the consistency and robustness of the estimators. Results suggest that conventional socioeconomic gradients are statistical artifacts, fully mediated by subjective health, with heterogeneous effects across sexes. Moreover, the estimations confirm the transversal importance of family support in subjective well-being. We further uncover pronounced sex-dimorphism: in men, a distinct biosignature (testosterone, NTRK2, cholesterol) and a high-risk "metabolically-vulnerable stoic" phenotype emerge, whereas in women these signals are attenuated, pointing to divergent biological pathways. The methodological framework uncovers previously latent pathways, establishing immune dysregulation (SELL, CRTAM, GZMA), neuroplasticity deficits (UNC5C, GDNF, SFRP3), and the kynurenine metabolic pathway (HDL, KYNU) as key factors associated with mental health risks. These results provide compelling evidence for a paradigmatic shift toward policy approaches that integrate biomarker-informed risk stratification into both health and mental health policy frameworks.

title: I Phone -17  Need or Luxury in India

detail.title: I Phone -17  Need or Luxury in India

detail.abstract: This paper will Examine the fact about need of I-phone 17, mandatory or just show off for Indians. The iPhone 17 in India represents the intersection of technological advancement and consumer aspiration. Equipped with cutting-edge features-such as the A19 chip, high-refresh-rate display, and advanced camera systems-it offers longterm reliability and strong resale value. However, with prices starting above ₹80,000, it is financially out of reach for the majority of Indian consumers. For basic communication and media use, cheaper alternatives provide comparable utility, positioning the iPhone 17 largely as a luxury product. Yet for professionals, creators, and heavy users who demand performance, durability, and ecosystem integration, it may be justified as a functional need. Thus, in the Indian context, the iPhone 17 is primarily a luxury, but situationally it can evolve into a practical necessity.

title: Production Networks and R&D Allocation
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Department of Economics and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)

detail.title: Production Networks and R&D Allocation
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how production networks shape firms' R&D decisions and the resulting aggregate inefficiencies. We develop a dynamic model in which firms form supplier relationships through an exogenous yet persistent matching process and rely on those links to introduce new products. The model features two sources of misallocation: market-power distortions and a network-formation externality whereby firms fail to internalize that their R&D makes them more attractive trading partners, improving match quality for all firms in the economy. We estimate the model using Japanese firm-to-firm transaction and patent data and show that the first-best allocation lies close to the decentralized outcome. Market-power corrections raise R&D incentives for older firms by relieving double marginalization along long supply chains. Internalizing the network-formation externality instead tilts R&D toward younger firms that expand their supplier base most rapidly. These opposing forces offset each other, leaving the planner's allocation near the observed one.

title: Solving the Legal Riddle of Financial Insitutions
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Solving the Legal Riddle of Financial Insitutions

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Law and Financial Studies, 2020

detail.abstract: This article examines the persistent problem of law to address financial institutional failure and the mechanisms proposed to address it: tort liability, laissez-faire markets, and government regulation. Drawing from economic theory, legal scholarship, and historical examples such as tulip mania, the analysis evaluates the effectiveness of each approach in ensuring stability and protecting consumers. Tort law, while centered on justice and deterrence, proves costly, inefficient, and stifling to financial innovation. A free-market approach fosters creativity but fails to prevent destructive cycles of speculation and collapse. By contrast, regulation—when carefully designed, as with the Glass-Steagall Act—emerges as the most effective means of reducing systemic risk, preserving market confidence, and safeguarding consumers. Ultimately, the article argues that law and regulation are indispensable for shaping the environment of financial institutions and preventing predictable failures driven by short-term profit motives.

title: The Road to Serfdom Framework: Hayek’s Critique of France’s Centralized Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic

detail.title: The Road to Serfdom Framework: Hayek’s Critique of France’s Centralized Response to the COVID-19 Pandemic

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests. The views expressed are solely those of the author, and no proprietary or confidential data were used.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a conceptual/policy analysis based on publicly available sources; it did not involve human participants, patient data, interventions.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding. This research received no specific grant from any funding agency, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: This article offers a Hayekian analysis of France's response to the COVID-19 crisis, exploring the tension between spontaneous order and centralized planning in a systemic, international crisis context. Drawing on Hayek's insights, we examine the difficulty for social scientists to conceptualize spontaneous and constructed orders in moments of emergency, where the pressure for immediate state intervention often obscures decentralized alternatives. We then turn to the specificity of the French case, arguing that France's intensely bureaucratic and centralized political elite makes it uniquely susceptible to planning pitfalls. This article offers a novel theoretical contribution by systematically applying the structure of Hayek's book, The Road to Serfdom, to the analysis of France's COVID-19 crisis management, what I would call in The Road to Serfdom Framework. By following the book's key chapters, this study transposes Hayek's arguments on the dangers of centralization and planning to the pandemic response, introducing, for the first time in the literature, a methodology that highlights the pitfalls of state centralization through a Hayekian lens. Hayek was particularly critical of France's legal tradition and conception of liberalism, shaped by rationalist and dirigiste intellectual currents that prioritize state intervention over emergent social order. This institutional legacy explains the rigid, top-down structure of France's pandemic management, which we document through an analysis of key public policy measures implemented during the crisisranging from lockdowns to emergency decrees and the extension of executive powers.

title: Click, Code, Earn: The Returns to Digital Skills
affiliations: World Bank, , World Bank Group and World Bank

detail.title: Click, Code, Earn: The Returns to Digital Skills
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first comprehensive, crosscountry evidence on the wage returns to digital skills using over 67 million job postings from 29 countries between 2021 and 2024. We develop a harmonized digital skills taxonomy and examine returns across extensive (any digital skill required), intensive (number of digital skills), and qualitative (type of digital skill) margins. Digital skills command substantial wage premiums globally, with particularly pronounced returns in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs) where such competencies remain scarce. Requiring at least one digital skill raises advertised wages by 1.6% on average, with returns of 1.3% in high-income countries (HICs) and 7.5% in LMICs. Each additional digital skill increases wages by 0.5% in HICs and 2.6% in LMICs, while intermediate and advanced skills yield even higher premiums of 0.8% in HICs and 3% in LMICs. Each traditional AI skills offer returns of 2.9% across all countries. Most remarkably, generative AI (GenAI) skills demonstrate the highest premiums: GenAI development skills command 7-9% wage increases in technical occupations, while GenAI literacy skills yield sizable premiums of 25-36% in non-technical professional roles, reflecting both their productivity potential and current scarcity. Returns are consistently higher in digitally intensive industries and occupations, and are amplified by workers' education and experience, suggesting strong complementarities between digital competencies and traditional human capital. These findings highlight the critical importance of digital skills for individual earnings and economic development, particularly in LMICs.

title: Majoritarian Signals: Harnessing Genai To Inform Judicial Standards
affiliations: Tel Aviv University, The Buchmann Faculty of Law and

detail.title: Majoritarian Signals: Harnessing Genai To Inform Judicial Standards
detail.abstract: This Article offers a systematic framework for incorporating majoritarian signals from generative AI (GenAI) foundation models into legal adjudication. While legal scholars have traditionally viewed GenAI's embedded social biases as a normative flaw, this Article reframes them as potentially valuable evidentiary proxies for interpreting vague or open-ended legal standards. When carefully interrogated, majoritarian signals-patterns that reflect the most common uses, norms, or expectations in language and culture-can illuminate the shared understandings that underlie core legal doctrines. Drawing on insights from computational social science, the Article demonstrates how GenAI models trained on vast cultural corpora capture statistical regularities that mirror prevailing beliefs, practices, and linguistic conventions. These signals, it argues, can help courts approximate the meaning of terms like "reasonable care," "ordinary meaning," "genericity," and "originality"-standards that frequently rely on implicit majoritarian reasoning but lack reliable empirical tools for application. The Article proceeds in two parts. Part I develops the theoretical foundation, tracing the emergence of majoritarian reasoning in computational research and extending it to legal interpretation. It identifies and critically assesses three challenges to integrating GenAI signals into judicial decision-making: normative, methodological, and procedural. Part II applies this framework to two prominent legal contexts where majoritarian reasoning plays a central role-contract interpretation and copyright scope analysis. It offers concrete methodologies for extracting relevant signals, such as autocompletion and inpainting, and outlines procedural safeguards to ensure their responsible use. By responsibly integrating these tools, courts may improve the transparency, consistency, and fairness of adjudication in an increasingly data-driven legal landscape.

title: Digital Assets as Safe Havens Portfolio Diversification Benefits Across Crisis and Post-COVID Periods
affiliations: The University of Lahore Islamabad Campus

detail.title: Digital Assets as Safe Havens Portfolio Diversification Benefits Across Crisis and Post-COVID Periods

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animals; therefore, ethics approval was not required.

detail.abstract: This study examines the safe-haven potential and portfolio diversification benefits of digital assets across two phases of global financial uncertainty: the COVID-19 crisis (January 2020-December 2021) and the post-COVID recovery (January 2022-December 2023). Focusing on Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and two stablecoins (USDC and USDT), the analysis employs descriptive statistics, correlation matrices, and GARCH(1,1) models to assess return dynamics, volatility clustering, and persistence. The results show that Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced significant volatility and long-lasting shock persistence during the COVID period, limiting their effectiveness as safe havens. In the post-COVID phase, volatility persistence declined, reflecting improved resilience, though both assets remained speculative and risk-sensitive relative to traditional hedging instruments. By contrast, stablecoins behaved consistently as low-variance assets. USDC maintained near-zero conditional variance throughout, apart from a brief fluctuation in mid-2021, while USDT displayed a short but pronounced volatility spike linked to confidence issues before quickly stabilizing. Overall, the findings indicate that cryptocurrencies function more as high-risk diversifiers than genuine safe havens, whereas stablecoins provide stronger hedging characteristics and can enhance portfolio stability. These results have important implications for investors, portfolio managers, and regulators in developing risk management strategies and integrating digital assets into financial stability frameworks.

title: Nurse Practitioner Training and Local Medical Provider Supply
affiliations: University of Wyoming, University of Wyoming, Michigan State University and Texas A&M University

detail.title: Nurse Practitioner Training and Local Medical Provider Supply
detail.abstract: The Nurse Practitioner (NP) workforce expanded rapidly from 2010-2023, especially in rural counties, where patients today are nearly as likely to receive care from an NP as from a physician. At the same time, rural health outcomes and access to health care continue to worsen relative to urban areas. Empirical research on how NPs interact with or substitute for physicians remains limited. This paper exploits county-level openings of graduate nursing programs to test how they impact the local supply of NPs and primary care physicians. Using data from the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) and Area Health Resource File (AHRF), we estimate staggered difference-in-differences frameworks. We show that new graduate programs in Health Professional Shortage Area (HPSA) designated counties are particularly effective in translating program completions into increased NP supply. We find that over the decade after a program first graduates students, 30% of students remain in the county, increasing the level of NPs by as much as 8% annually in HPSA counties. We show positive spatial spillover effects for rural counties nearby a county with a new program. We find no adverse impact of local NP increases on the number of primary care physicians, suggesting that broader access to NP education boosts the local supply of providers overall. This paper illustrates the importance of rural medical education in increasing local access to primary care providers and in addressing existing inequities in access to care.

title: From Questionnaires to Eye-Tracking: Rethinking the Future of ASD Screeners

detail.title: From Questionnaires to Eye-Tracking: Rethinking the Future of ASD Screeners

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author (H.D.) is CTO, co-founder and a shareholder of EyeContact Dx Ltd., which develops webcam-based eye-tracking software for early autism screening. The topic of this perspective is related to the company’s area of work. No other competing interests are declared.
declarations.funderStatement: No specific funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Early autism spectrum disorder (ASD) screening is dominated by caregiver questionnaires whose reported accuracy is typically benchmarked against unstable diagnostic labels at 16-24 months and study designs prone to partial verification. We suggest that common design features can overestimate real-world performance and obscure trade-offs. In particular, three common features-(i) diagnostic instability across early development, (ii) selective diagnostic follow-up and case-enrichment (e.g., overrepresentation of "clearly ASD" children among those evaluated), and (iii) dependence of headline metrics on the underlying prevalence and proportion flagged-combine to make published sensitivity/specificity figures poor guides for clinical practice and unreliable for comparing screeners across studies, sites, or thresholds. We further note a domain mismatch: questionnaires infer risk from coarse caregiver report, whereas decisions increasingly require objective, fine-grained measures of early social attention and behavior. We propose a staged validation approach. In the near term, evaluate hybrid screeners that pair objective behavioral measurement (e.g., eye-tracking) with caregiver questionnaires against best-judgment clinical diagnosis at 18-24 months, while reporting positive-screen rates and follow-up completeness. In parallel, pre-specify ≥36-month outcomes and transition primary validation to longitudinal endpoints over the next 2-3 years. This balances feasibility now with the longer-run goal of clinically meaningful prediction. This perspective shifts emphasis from short-term label agreement to clinically meaningful prediction, aiming to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity so limited developmental resources reach the children most likely to benefit.

title: The Mirage of Measuring the Performance of Delta-Hedged Option Strategies
affiliations: VinUniversity

detail.title: The Mirage of Measuring the Performance of Delta-Hedged Option Strategies
detail.abstract:
Delta-hedged option strategies are commonly evaluated by comparing implied variance at inception with realised
variance over the contract’s life. This paper shows that such a benchmark is fundamentally flawed. The finite number
of return observations within an option’s maturity is far too small to ensure convergence of realised variance estimators
to the true integrated variance, especially once volatility clustering and jumps are accounted for. Numerical analysis
reveals that the effective sample size implied by realistic maturities collapses so sharply that achieving the precision
suggested by iid benchmarks would require decades of data, an unattainable horizon for traded options. The supposed
accuracy of realised variance is therefore an illusion created by misapplied asymptotics. By contrasting market
practice with the correct statistical perspective grounded in ergodicity and long-run variance estimation, this paper
bridges financial economics and volatility econometrics, and argues that performance attribution of delta-hedged
option strategies cannot rely on realised variance as a stable benchmark.

title: How Ketamine Became an Antidepressant

detail.title: How Ketamine Became an Antidepressant

publicationDetails.detailsText: Berkeley Technology Law journal, Volume 39, Pp. 499-552; DOI: 10.15779/Z38W08WH8B

detail.abstract: Ketamine’s path from anesthetic to antidepressant reframed treatment-resistant depression (TRD) by shifting focus from monoamines to glutamate/NMDA modulation. This Article traces the science (from Yale–NIMH pilot work through Zarate 2006), synthesizes evidence across routes of administration (IV, IM, oral, sublingual, intranasal) with bioavailability tradeoffs, and explains why esketamine (Spravato) became the only FDA-approved ketamine-based therapy for TRD. It analyzes how patents, FDA approval standards (placebo vs. active comparator), DEA Schedule III controls, and payer coverage collectively shaped access, pricing, and clinical uptake—while off-label racemic ketamine and telehealth channels expanded use outside the Spravato REMS clinic model. The Article then surveys innovation pressures (startups, at-home protocols, and next-generation glutamatergic agents/HNK metabolites) and policy choices that could better align safety, evidence, and affordability. Tables summarize post-Zarate TRD outcomes and route-of-administration pharmacokinetics; another contrasts DEA scheduling for common antidepressants, situating ketamine’s unique risk/benefit profile. The takeaway: ketamine catalyzed a new antidepressant paradigm, but U.S. IP, regulatory, and insurance incentives—not science alone—determine who benefits and at what cost.

title: Soulbound Tokens, Identity, and Depolarizing Social Media
affiliations: Stanford University

detail.title: Soulbound Tokens, Identity, and Depolarizing Social Media
detail.abstract: Online discourse today is plagued by toxic content and polarization, amplified by the ease of anonymity and fake accounts. This paper investigates whether tying social media profiles to verifiable real-world identities via blockchain-based soulbound tokens (SBTs) and related decentralized identity tools can simultaneously reduce online incivility and curb polarization. Stronger identity and reputation signals can deter the worst abuses (e.g. overt threats, hate speech), as users face greater reputational risk when not purely anonymous. While research shows that anonymity fuels disinhibition and uncivil behavior, and thus verification should increase baseline civility, identity verification alone is not a panacea for ideological polarization. Nonetheless, privacy-preserving decentralized identity systems, anchored on an SBT identity stack, offers a step forward towards improving civil discourse.

title: Amicus Brief of Professor Peter Swire in Support of the Independence of the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board
affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology

detail.title: Amicus Brief of Professor Peter Swire in Support of the Independence of the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board

declarations.funderStatement: Georgia Tech School of Cybersecurity and Privacy

contentType.other: Filed in court as a public document

publicationDetails.detailsText: Amicus Brief, U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit

detail.abstract:
This document is an amicus brief filed by Professor Peter Swire in his personal capacity, supporting the independence of members of the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board (PCLOB). In early 2025, President Trump issued the order to remove three members of the Board. The orders were not “for cause” – there was no statement of any wrongdoing by the members. In the district court, the judge found, based on the statute creating the PCLOB, that the PCLOB is an independent agency whose members can lawfully only be fired for cause. The U.S. Department of Justice appealed the case, and Swire submitted this brief in support of PCLOB independence.

   The brief explains that the PCLOB is a unique agency to address the fundamental constitutional tension between liberty and security. It plays a unique role in responding to the history of constitutional violations under secret U.S. government surveillance programs, and the independence of the PCLOB is clearly established by the history of its founding statute.

   There is a distinct Fourth Amendment analysis for secret foreign intelligence surveillance, supporting the independence of the PCLOB. The PCLOB oversees reasonableness of the Fourth Amendment. Changes in technology and surveillance targets are an important feature of secret government surveillance, calling for the continual review provided by the PCLOB.  The independence of the PCLOB protects Fourth Amendment reasonableness and is constitutionally relevant to this case. 

   The U.S. government has had a longstanding and previously-unbroken position that the PCLOB is independent. Notably, the U.S Government and European legal authorities have emphasized the independence of the PCLOB, in litigation before European courts and in diplomatic negotiations for the EU/U.S. Data Privacy Framework, which according to the U.S. Government applies to $7 trillion of annual trade between the EU and the U.S.

title: Market Power From an Economic Perspective: A Competition Lawyer’s Guided Tour
affiliations: Nova School of Law

detail.title: Market Power From an Economic Perspective: A Competition Lawyer’s Guided Tour
detail.abstract: The notion of market power stands at the centre of competition law, although the notion itself can be understood in different ways. Two of those ways were directly borrowed from microeconomics: market power as the ability to price profitably above the competitive level (Chicago School); and market power as the ability to exclude competitors from the market (post-Chicago scholarship). This contribution proposes to explore the microeconomic notion of market power from the perspective of a competition lawyer who, wanting a formal training in economics, is nevertheless set to understand the content, scope, rationale and limits of this notion.

title: Extreme Events in Corporate Bond Spreads
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Extreme Events in Corporate Bond Spreads
detail.abstract: The market value of corporate bonds was equivalent to around a third of global GDP as of 2024. It represents a key asset class for professional and private investors. However, it is subject to high volatility and is very sensitive to rare but extreme events, such as the financial and Covid-19 crises. We study the extremal behaviour of corporate bond spreads in the United States and in the Euro Area across different rating segments and sectors. We base our study on three decades of daily data. We control for financial and macroeconomic variables that are likely to affect spreads. Our approach uses three different methods from Extreme Value Theory (EVT). It focuses first on the marginal distributions of corporate bond spreads, then models the bivariate tail dependence structure of cross-regional and cross-market corporate bond spreads and finally on the distribution of corporate bond spreads over time, capturing their volatility dynamics as well as their heavy tails. During crisis periods, the degree of dependence is surprisingly high, suggesting a contagion effect. Our fitted models show that more standard approaches would massively underestimate the probabilities of rare events and that the combination of dynamic volatility modelling with EVT is robust and well suited for extrapolating risk measures beyond the maximum level of corporate bond spreads observed in the historical data.

title: TRMTrack:Trajectory robust maintenance in online Multi-Object tracking
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: TRMTrack:Trajectory robust maintenance in online Multi-Object tracking
detail.abstract: Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) represents a research task of significant value in computer vision. In practical scenarios, frequent inter-object occlusions pose substantial challenges, making it difficult to maintain stable tracking through simple feature association alone. Existing studies typically employ post-processing methods, such as linear interpolation, to infer object positions during occlusion periods to maintain trajectory continuity. However, these offline post-processing approaches not only contradict the real-time requirements of tracking tasks but also tend to introduce additional false positive (FP) tracking results. To address the tracking challenges during occlusion periods, this paper proposes a novel online tracker called TRMTrack, built upon the widely-adopted Tracking-By-Detection (TBD) paradigm and based on stable tracking duration. Compared to existing TBD methods, TRMTrack maintains predictions of occluded objects through an innovative plug-and-play lifecycle management mechanism in a fully online manner. To enhance prediction accuracy, we develop two key modules within TRMTrack. The Trajectory Reconstruction module mitigates detection noise impact by reconstructing object trajectories prior to observation loss, while the Adaptive Trajectory Prediction mechanism dynamically integrates long-term and short-term motion information based on the duration of observation loss. Our approach relies exclusively on motion cues for trajectory prediction, eliminating the need for post-processing methods to complete missing object positions during occlusions. Extensive experiments on MOT17 and MOT20 benchmark datasets demonstrate significant improvements in tracking performance, achieving 1.6% and 1.2% increases in HOTA metrics respectively, along with superior performance in IDF1 and AssA metrics compared to existing post-processing methods.

title: Optimal Markdown Pricing with Patient Customers
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) and National University of Singapore (NUS)

detail.title: Optimal Markdown Pricing with Patient Customers
detail.abstract: In contemporary applications, the implementation of dynamic pricing is often challenged by pricing constraints and non-myopic customer behaviours. This paper studies the dynamic pricing problem with practical constraints including inventory, markdown, price change constraint, and with consideration of the patient customer behavior. Despite the complex customer demand models, we show that the optimal revenue can be achieved by a dynamic pricing policy that determines the posted price based at a time period, based on the current level of inventory and the prices offered in previous periods. We construct the dynamic pricing policies by solving a set of certain "modified" Bellman equations, which involves constructing the expected reward and transition probability in each period judiciously to capture patient customers' demands. The "modified" Bellman equations help us overcome the curse of dimensionality of the problem. We offer operational insights into the amount of inventory to order before sales and the desirable number of markdowns. Indeed, our empirical results consistently exhibit the decreasing marginal return with inventory and markdown numbers. In addition, we also provide insights into the optimal timing of markdowns with increasing customers' patient level-the decision makers should markdown later with more patient customers.

title: Blockchain Technology as a Quality Assurance Mechanism in Asymmetric Information Duopolies
affiliations: and University of Edinburgh

detail.title: Blockchain Technology as a Quality Assurance Mechanism in Asymmetric Information Duopolies
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how blockchain technology can serve as an effective quality assurance mechanism in duopoly markets characterized by asymmetric information. We develop a dynamic game-theoretic model of a duopoly in which firms compete on product quality under conditions of limited observability. The model incorporates adaptive consumer learning, brand loyalty heterogeneity, and probabilistic firm strategies over quality levels. A Stackelberg structure is introduced to capture sequential decision-making, with one firm acting as a strategic leader. The framework is extended by embedding blockchain-enabled transparency and disclosure mechanisms, allowing firms to credibly signal quality through immutable verification. Simulation results demonstrate that in the absence of blockchain, strategic randomization leads to unstable mixed-strategy equilibria and diminished consumer welfare. Conversely, blockchain adoption enhances consumer trust, incentivizes consistent high-quality provision, and stabilizes competitive dynamics. The findings reveal that blockchain acts not merely as a technological upgrade but as a transformative governance mechanism that shifts firms from opportunistic price-based competition to sustainable quality-centric strategies. The study also explores conditions under which transparency mitigates adverse selection and redefines consumer-firm interactions. Sensitivity analyses further highlight the interplay between learning rates, brand bias, and the effectiveness of blockchain in restoring market efficiency.

title: Transportation and Transmission: The Role of Railways in Shaping Mortality Patterns in British India *
affiliations: Department of Economics

detail.title: Transportation and Transmission: The Role of Railways in Shaping Mortality Patterns in British India *
detail.abstract: How does transportation infrastructure affect public health in developing economies? This paper examines the impact of railway expansion on communicable disease mortality in colonial India's Bombay Presidency (1885-1919). Using townlevel mortality data for cholera, smallpox, and plague, combined with a spatially weighted railway density measure for each town, we estimate panel data fixed effects regressions. We find an inverted U-shaped relationship: mortality peaked at moderate railway density (log density ≈ 2.95), suggesting that initial railway expansion increased disease transmission through enhanced mobility and connectivity, but mortality declined at higher densities, consistent with improved access to medical care and food supplies. Robustness checks, including spatial clustering and placebo tests for non-communicable mortality, confirm this non-linearity. These findings contribute to the infrastructure and development literature by showing that transportation networks exhibit non-monotonic health effects, challenging the linear relationships assumed in previous studies and reconciling conflicting evidence on whether colonial railways were beneficial or harmful to population health.

title: Reservoir-driven Parameters
affiliations: University of Verona - Department of Economics

detail.title: Reservoir-driven Parameters
detail.abstract: Inspired by the reservoir computing paradigm in machine learning, we introduce a new class of observation-driven time series models in which the time-varying parameters are reconstructed from a high-dimensional basis of randomly generated states, called reservoirs. This design can be viewed as a recurrent neural network where only the output layer is trained, while the internal weights are randomly sampled and remain fixed. Compared to existing observation-driven models, the proposed method offers several key advantages: a) it can approximate in L^p sense any causal time-invariant filter; b) the invertibility condition is feasible and invariant across model specifications; c) the gradient and Hessian of the likelihood function are available in closed form, making the method computationally efficient and well suited for multivariate applications. The inferential theory of the quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is established by deriving conditions for consistency and asymptotic normality. Using simulated and empirical data, we show that the method outperforms alternative observation-driven specifications in recovering highly nonlinear parameter dynamics, including jumps, structural breaks, and chaotic behavior.

title: Air Quality and Conferences' Engagement
affiliations: University of Warwick, , University of Oxford, Universidad del Rosario, Universidad del Rosario - Faculty of Economics and University of Warwick

detail.title: Air Quality and Conferences' Engagement
detail.abstract: There is limited evidence on the non-health impacts of air pollution, including productivity in the workplace and behavior. We examine the effect of air pollution on participation, collaboration, and feedback provision in a workplace setting. Our experiment randomly assigns air purifiers to rooms at three large academic conferences to investigate the causal impact of air pollution on participants' engagement behavior. We construct a participant engagement index based on 12 presentation-level behavioral outcomes directly measured by conference observers through an online form and weigh each behavioral outcome using weights elicited from an expert survey. Conference rooms treated with air purifiers exhibit 48% less PM 2.5 concentration compared to control rooms. However, we do not find a statistically significant change in engagement. Communication in the workplace might not be a large driver of the empirical relationship between air quality and productivity, albeit more research is needed across workplaces and measures of communication.

title: Increase Alpha: Performance and Risk of an AI-Driven Trading Framework
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Kent - Kent Business School and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Increase Alpha: Performance and Risk of an AI-Driven Trading Framework
detail.abstract: There are inefficiencies in the financial market, leaving unexploited patterns embedded in price, volume, and cross-sectional relationships. While recent advances increasingly employ large-scale transformer architectures, we take a domain-focused route: classical feedforward and recurrent networks paired with expertly curated features to mine subtle regularities in noisy financial data. This smaller-footprint design is computationally lean and reliable under low signal-to-noise conditions-qualities that matter for daily production at scale. At Increase Alpha, we developed a deep-learning framework that maps a universe of over 800 U.S. equities into daily directional signals with minimal computational overhead. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we outline the general overview of the predictive model without disclosing its core underlying concepts. Second, we evaluate its real-time performance through transparent, industry standard metrics. Forecast accuracy is benchmarked against both naive baselines and macro indicators. The performance outcomes are summarized via cumulative returns, annualized Sharpe ratio, and maximum drawdown. The best portfolio combination using our signals provides a low-risk, continuous stream of returns with a Sharpe ratio of more than 2.5, maximum drawdown of around 3%, and a near-zero correlation with the S&P 500 market benchmark. We also compare the model's performance through different market regimes, such as the recent volatile movements of the US equity market in the beginning of 2025. Our analysis showcases the robustness of the model and significantly stable performance during these volatile periods. Collectively, these findings show that market inefficiencies can be systematically harvested with modest computational overhead if the right variables are considered. This report will emphasize the potential of traditional deep learning frameworks for generating an AI-driven edge in the financial market.

title: Copyright and Competition: Estimating Supply and Demand with Unstructured Data
affiliations: and University of Texas at Austin - Department of Economics

detail.title: Copyright and Competition: Estimating Supply and Demand with Unstructured Data
detail.abstract: We study the competitive and welfare effects of copyright in creative industries in the face of cost-reducing technologies such as generative artificial intelligence. Creative products often feature unstructured attributes (e.g., images and text) that are complex and high-dimensional. To address this challenge, we study a stylized design product-fonts-using data from the world's largest font marketplace. We construct neural network embeddings to quantify unstructured attributes and measure visual similarity in a manner consistent with human perception. Spatial regression and event-study analyses demonstrate that competition is local in the visual characteristics space. Building on this evidence, we develop a structural model of supply and demand that incorporates embeddings and captures product positioning under copyright-based similarity constraints. Our estimates reveal consumers' heterogeneous design preferences and producers' cost-effective mimicry advantages. Counterfactual analyses show that copyright protection can raise consumer welfare by encouraging product relocation, and that the optimal policy depends on the interaction between copyright and cost-reducing technologies.

title: Factors Related to Workers' Engagement in Readymade Garment Industry of Bangladesh
affiliations: Uttara University and Bangladesh University of Business and Technology

detail.title: Factors Related to Workers' Engagement in Readymade Garment Industry of Bangladesh

keywords: Worker Access to Learning and Good Career Opportunity

detail.abstract: Workers' engagement refers to the organizational conditions where all the members of an organization are committed to their organization's goals and values, motivated to contribute to organizational success with an enhanced sense of their own well-being (Little & Little, 2006). Positive engagement is expected by any organization because it makes workers well connected with their jobs, loyal, and increase willing to put extra effort to do their jobs just to accomplish their goals in the company. Readymade garment (RMG) industry of Bangladesh is the main earner of foreign currency that consists of more than 75% of the country's export earnings. But the workers of this industry are often found unengaged at their work due to the ill behavior of their supervisors, poor working conditions, lack of organization incentives, and the absence of motivational policies of the companies. Hence, this study aims at identifying the workers' engagement factors of RMG industry of Bangladesh. This study interviewed 319 RMG workers from ten leading garment companies. Descriptive and inferential statistical techniques were used to analyze the data. Results show that the RMG workers' engagement factors are: feeling the company as a great company, feeling proud and recommend others, access to learning and good career opportunity, knowing the development of the company, quality supervision and recognition for good jobs done, and manager cares the workers. This study suggests that the RMG policymakers should focus more on the supervision styles of the managers and appreciating policy of the companies that can help improving the engagement level of the workers in this industry of Bangladesh.

title: Development and Validation of a Currency Convertibility Risk Indicator for Brazil: The IRCB Framework

detail.title: Development and Validation of a Currency Convertibility Risk Indicator for Brazil: The IRCB Framework
detail.abstract: This paper introduces the Brazilian Currency Convertibility Risk Indicator (IRCB-Indicador de Risco de Conversibilidade Brasileiro), a novel composite index designed to assess and predict the likelihood of capital control implementation in Brazil. The IRCB aggregates five critical dimensions: fiscal situation (25%), external accounts (30%), exchange rate pressures (25%), regulatory environment (10%), and market indicators (10%). Using a comprehensive dataset spanning January 2015 to June 2025, we validate the indicator's effectiveness in capturing convertibility risk dynamics during significant economic events, including the COVID-19 pandemic, political transitions, and external shocks. The indicator successfully identified critical risk periods, with values exceeding 70 points preceding the implementation of major capital control measures. Our findings suggest that the IRCB provides policymakers and market participants with a robust early warning system for convertibility risks, achieving an accuracy rate of 87.3% in predicting control implementations within a 30-day window when the indicator exceeds the critical threshold. The framework's real-time monitoring capabilities, implemented via a RESTful API, enable continuous risk assessment, contributing to more informed decisionmaking in emerging market currency management.

title:
Benchmarking Financial Performance Across

Hospital Chains
affiliations: Ladoke Akintola University of Technology

detail.title:
Benchmarking Financial Performance Across

Hospital Chains

keywords: Techniques To Identify Best Practices and Performance Gaps.

detail.abstract: This study examines the financial performance of hospital chains by employing benchmarking techniques to identify best practices and performance gaps. The purpose of the research is to provide hospital administrators and policymakers with actionable insights that enhance operational efficiency, profitability, and strategic decision-making. A quantitative methodology was adopted, analyzing financial statements and key performance indicators (KPIs) across multiple hospital chains over a five-year period. Benchmarking metrics included revenue growth, cost management, profitability ratios, and return on investment. The key findings reveal significant variation in financial performance across hospital chains, highlighting the impact of management strategies, scale, and operational efficiency. The study demonstrates that benchmarking not only facilitates comparative analysis but also supports the adoption of practices that improve financial sustainability and competitiveness in the healthcare sector.

title: The Evolution of Biodiversity in Corporate Discourse: Evidence from Large Language Model-Assisted Frame Analysis
affiliations: University of Amsterdam - Department of Political Science

detail.title: The Evolution of Biodiversity in Corporate Discourse: Evidence from Large Language Model-Assisted Frame Analysis
detail.abstract: Nature and biodiversity are declining at unprecedented rates. Corporations in the agrifood, construction, and mining sectors disproportionately affect ecosystems while shaping global supply chains and sustainability governance. This paper examines how the most powerful firms in these sectors articulate the values of nature in their sustainability discourse. The question of values is central: many scholars argue that a values crisis underpins the biodiversity emergency, with economic framings dominating while ecological, intrinsic, and socio-cultural perspectives are marginalized. Such narrowing risks undermining both the legitimacy and effectiveness of biodiversity governance. Recognizing and engaging with value pluralism is therefore viewed as essential for transformative change. Drawing on 2,139 corporate sustainability reports published between 2014 and 2023, and combining large language models with human-coded validation, the analysis shows that economic framings remain dominant in corporate discourse. Yet there are emerging signs of diversification, suggesting a gradual – though still limited – broadening of the valuation corridor. Mining companies display the most pronounced diversification, agrifood firms adopt more ecological framings, while construction remains largely confined to economic rationales. These findings highlight how corporate responses to biodiversity are uneven, shaped by sectoral political-economic dynamics, and raise doubts about the depth of corporate engagement with value pluralism.

title: (Visualizing) Plausible Treatment Effect Paths
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business - Econometrics and Statistics

detail.title: (Visualizing) Plausible Treatment Effect Paths

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Philadelphia Working Paper No. 25-27
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: We consider estimation and inference for treatment effect paths. Examples include dynamic treatment effects, impulse response functions, and event study paths. We present two sets of plausible bounds to help visualize uncertainty associated with these paths. Both plausible bounds are often tighter than traditional confidence intervals, and can provide insights even when traditional (uniform) confidence bands appear uninformative. Our first set of bounds covers the average (or overall) effect rather than the entire path. Our second set of bounds imposes data-driven smoothness restrictions on the treatment path, using post-selection inference (Berk et al. [2013]) to provide formal coverage guarantees.
